cards.text: John's writing to believers, and he calls them children. He opens BIG: it is the last hour, and they've heard that the antichrist is coming. Friend, that is NOT a snooze-button announcement.

cards.question: The believers have heard the antichrist is coming. What does John say has already happened?

cards.text: John says that's how they know it's the last hour. Then he says something about these antichrists that hits a little too close to home.

cards.question: True or false: John says these antichrists went out from among the believers.

cards.text: They were with the believers, and then they walked out. You ever have somebody leave the group chat? Nobody needs a speech. That little notice says EVERYTHING.

cards.question: John says that if those people had really belonged to the believers, they would have ___ with them.

cards.text: Their leaving made it clear none of them belonged. Then John turns back to the believers, and his whole tone changes. This part is GOOD news.

cards.question: What does John say the believers have from the Holy One?
True or false: John says he's writing to the believers because they don't know the truth yet.

cards.text: John says no lie comes from the truth. Then he asks who the liar is, and he does not leave you hanging. No cliffhanger. No 'tune in next week.' He just says it.

cards.question: Who does John call the liar?

answers.text: Whoever denies that Jesus is the Christ

cards.question: John says the antichrist is the one who denies the ___ and the ___.
True or false: John says a person can deny the Son and still have the Father.

cards.text: Whoever confesses the Son has the Father as well. Now John gives the believers their job, and it comes with a promise attached.

cards.question: What does John tell the believers to let remain in them?

answers.text: What they heard from the beginning
The words of the ones who left

cards.question: If that message remains in them, they'll remain in the Son and in the Father. And the promise He Himself made to them is eternal ___.

cards.text: Eternal life. Baker, I spent years in a junk drawer next to an expired coupon that still believed in itself. THIS promise? Does. Not. Expire. Then John tells them why he's been writing all this.

cards.question: True or false: John says he has written these things about those who are trying to deceive the believers.

cards.text: Last word, and John comes back to that anointing. It remains in them, they don't need anyone to teach them, and His true and genuine anointing teaches them about all things.

cards.question: With that anointing teaching them, what does John tell the believers to do?

answers.text: Remain in Him as they were taught
Go bring back the ones who left
Find a new teacher to follow

findings.problem: The opening card names the writer as John, but 1 John 2:18-27 never names its author, so the card gives no reference for it. It also never says who John is. The docs allow outside facts like who wrote a letter only with their reference, and 1 John has no verse that names its writer.
findings.question: For a letter whose text never names its author, like 1 John, should Papa Dorin name the traditional author (John, one of Jesus' apostles) without a reference, or describe the writer without a name (for example, 'the writer')?

findings.problem: The card's first sentence repeats the answer to card 4 (they went out from the believers) and adds nothing new from the passage. The rest is a joke. Its only other content, that their departure made things clear, is told again on card 7. It also runs 4 sentences.
The story card is 4 sentences: 'They were with the believers, and then they walked out. You ever have somebody leave the group chat? Nobody needs a speech. That little notice says EVERYTHING.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card is 3 sentences: 'Their leaving made it clear none of them belonged. Then John turns back to the believers, and his whole tone changes. This part is GOOD news.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card is 5 sentences: 'John says no lie comes from the truth. Then he asks who the liar is, and he does not leave you hanging. No cliffhanger. No 'tune in next week.' He just says it.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card cites only 1 John 2:21, but it also tells that John asks who the liar is, which is 1 John 2:22. The citation should be 1 John 2:21-22.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The choice card tells a new piece of the passage inside its question: if the message remains in them, they will remain in the Son and in the Father (1 John 2:24). No story card tells this part. The card carries a story beat as well as its question. That beat belongs on a story card, which would also cite 1 John 2:24.

rule.text: A choice card is one question and its answers.

findings.problem: The story card is far more than 2 sentences: 'Eternal life. Baker, I spent years in a junk drawer next to an expired coupon that still believed in itself. THIS promise? Does. Not. Expire. Then John tells them why he's been writing all this.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 19, the setup right before this card, says the believers don't need anyone to teach them. That rules out the wrong answer 'Find a new teacher to follow' before the baker chooses.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The two blanks are 'Father' (blank 1) and 'Son' (blank 2). A baker who puts 'Son' in the first blank and 'Father' in the second has the same meaning, but would be marked wrong. The docs don't say whether two-blank answers must match the text's order or how to handle blanks whose words can swap.
findings.question: When the two right words of a two-blank card could swap places without changing the meaning, should either order be accepted, or should the card be rewritten so the order can't be argued?
